assembled_text: One of the best-known examples is Cheonmachong — the Tomb of the Heavenly Horse. It was excavated in 1973 as Tomb No. 155, during a test excavation before work on the much larger Hwangnamdaechong. More than eleven thousand objects were recovered, including a gold crown and a birch-bark saddle flap painted with a heavenly horse. That image gave the tomb the name we use today. But the person buried here is still not known with certainty. That uncertainty matters. History does not always give us a name — but the things people built and buried can still show us choices.
